_comment: The mutation gate's declaration: which files are mutation-graded, and which suites pin them. It is the only source for that pairing — the per-run Stryker config and the vitest include are both generated from it (`mutation-check.ts`), so there is no second list to keep in step. Entries arrive one at a time and deliberately: adding one asserts that the named suites, on their own, pin that file's behaviour, and the gate will say so in numbers on the next change to it. Asserted in full by `__tests__/mutation-scope.test.ts`, because a shrinking list is how this gate would pass by grading less.

equivalents.why: The guard exists to narrow `state` from `string | undefined` before it indexes the status map; it decides nothing the next line does not already decide. Without it an absent or empty state produces no mapped status, and `if (!externalStatus) return null` two lines down returns null for exactly the same inputs. No payload can tell the two apart, because there is none where the first guard returns and the second would not.

equivalents.line: if (highest === undefined || highest < count) known.executions.set(line, count)
equivalents.why: The comparison keeps the highest count a shard reported. With `<=` an equal count overwrites an equal count, which stores the same number it replaced. No input can distinguish the two, so no test can.

equivalents.line: if (best === undefined || best < count) executions.set(line, count)
equivalents.why: The same maximum, taken over the statements starting on one line. `<=` replaces an equal value with an equal value.

The component name is metadata on a log line and reaches no branch, no return value and no query. A test could only assert the string back from the logger it just configured, which is the tautology the mutation gate exists to expose rather than to reward.
Same line, same reason: the component name is log metadata, not behaviour. The line's operator-facing content that does matter — the post id in the warning — is asserted in post-source.db.test.ts.

The selected row is never read: hasActiveGitLabLink returns whether one came back, not what was in it. Narrowing or widening the projection cannot change that boolean, so no input distinguishes the two.

The guard only spares a throw the catch beside it absorbs: new URL rejects null, undefined and the empty string alike, and both paths end at the same gitlab.com default. Measured on all three falsy values.

Two constraints upstream already hold what the predicate checks: the query selects only mappings whose targetKey is this board, and completeRuleOf returns no rule unless filters.boardIds[0] equals that same targetKey. Every rule that reaches find therefore has boardId === boardId, so no stored row makes the predicate decide anything.
Only the number of queries changes. With no links, buildIssueMoveTargets returns the same empty list the short circuit returns, so the guard saves a lookup and decides nothing.

The shortcut and the general form build predicates that mean the same thing. Falling through yields `NOT assigned OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 ... AND <empty inArray>)`, and drizzle renders an empty `inArray` as the literal `false` (measured on 0.45.2), so the EXISTS is unsatisfiable and the OR collapses back to `NOT assigned` for every row. No entry, product or reader can be arranged where the two disagree, because they are the same predicate written twice. The branch is kept rather than deleted because the general form only reduces correctly through that empty-inArray rendering, which is drizzle's choice and not ours to rely on.

`defaultMessage` is the English written beside a message id, and react-intl reads it only when the active catalogue has no entry for that id. Every id in a shipped source file is in all nine catalogues -- that is what `bun scripts/i18n-check.ts` fails the build over -- so the catalogue always wins and this string never reaches a screen. A test could only assert it by rendering against a catalogue that lacks the id, which is the state the i18n gate exists to make impossible. It stays in the source as the fallback V6 promises if that gate ever stops holding, and because `bun run intl:extract` reads it.

The `$` follows a greedy `.*` that has already run to the end of the comment, and with `/s` there is no line boundary for it to stop at, so there is nothing left for the anchor to reject. Even a trailing newline the two could in principle disagree about is gone before anything reads the group: the only use of `matched[1]` trims it.

`start` is the offset of a comment, so `text[start]` is `/` and `text[start + 1]` is `*` or `/`. The backwards search for a newline therefore finds the same newline whether it begins one character before the comment or one character inside it, because a comment opens with two characters and neither of them can be a line break.

equivalents.line: const after = text.slice(end, lineEnd < 0 ? text.length : lineEnd)
equivalents.why: The branch is taken only when no newline follows the note, and what this line computes is read only through `ownLine`, which decides whether the note also speaks for the line below it. A line below exists only if a newline follows. So the mutant changes the answer exactly in the case where nothing can ask the question.

equivalents.line: const after = text.slice(end, lineEnd < 0 ? text.length : lineEnd)
equivalents.why: `lineEnd` is `indexOf('\n', end)` for a comment that ends past position 0, so it is either -1 or greater than 0. Zero is the one value the two comparisons disagree about, and it is the one value this search cannot return.

The fallback stands for a callee with no name of its own -- `window.self.alert`, where the object is itself a member expression -- and it is asked of a set holding one name. Any string that is not that name answers identically, so no source can tell the empty string from another absent name.

The same shape one line down, for a method reached by a computed key such as `toast['error']`, where the property has no name. The set holds three names and any other string answers the same, so the empty string is not distinguishable from another absent name.

Forced true, every node still reaching this line enters the branch, and the line inside it sends back an empty list for anything whose operator is not `+`. The one other node that carries `+` as an operator is a unary plus, which has no `left` and no `right`, so it spreads two empty lists -- the same empty list the fall-through below returns. The condition was split out of an `&&` for this record's sake: joined, three mutants shared the line and the manifest addresses a line by its text.

The component name is metadata on a log line and reaches no branch, no return value and no request. The operator-facing content of the hook's log lines — the project, the status and GitLab's answer — is asserted in hook.test.ts; the child's name is the one field a test could only read back from the logger it just configured.
Same line, same reason: the component name is log metadata, not behaviour, and the payload of every line the hook writes is asserted separately.

The second argument of history.replaceState is the entry's title, which the HTML specification tells browsers to ignore and no browser reads. The URL is the third argument and is asserted; nothing observable — not the location, not the history length, not the document title — changes with the second.
